rooms.title: Open-plan home
rooms.evidence: House number586, original hip roof, brick entry and large street tree explicitly connect original facade in95/162, site work213 and rebuilt facade. Same neighbouring house at right throughout.95 uniquely preserves intact original facade;162 preserves a distinct construction view not present in163/164. Original rear220, brick demolition219/218, X shoring215/200, excavations/foundations and finished106/84 share the distinctive pink gabled left neighbour, side access, original rear hip roof, fence and trees. The new addition shell and its large rear openings visibly connect the framing views. 216 shows basement excavation under existing masonry/joists;196/197 show the same stripped masonry shell with underfloor heating.178–180/190 show low basement ceiling, new partitions and concrete floor.98 uniquely supplies the completed basement and its stairwell exit alongside matching framing; retain the supplied collage intact. 223 and222 preserve the original main floor. Supplied comparisons113/114/116/166 explicitly link223,171/160 and132. Retained stair position, front entry/window, rear raised floor and original/new masonry openings connect the demolition, rough-in, drywall, floor installation and glass-balustrade views.182 main-floor front joists look toward the same front street tree and original entry. 222 is the existing kitchen beside the original stair.99 explicitly links156 to the completed kitchen100. Raised rear step, rear glass door, cabinet layout, two small high windows, distinctive ornate stone fireplace slab and shelving connect rough-in, cabinet installation and every finished kitchen angle.120/121 match kitchen cabinet crown moulding; exact photographed corner cannot independently establish the house, so these detail photos are flagged below. 155 firebox rough opening and152 installed diagonally veined slab exactly match131 and staged82/96. Same tall front window beside the projecting fireplace, ceiling speaker/light pattern and side passage.177 is horizontal fireplace framing, not bathroom framing; its exact final firebox position is less independently identifiable, so caption remains general. 181 and the construction portions of97/115 show the same stair opening, landing doors and upper-floor window. Finished133/137 match the comparison panels.185 shows the large street tree through the opened front upper-floor wall;186/187 show the adjoining original shell and stair opening.192 is an isolated masonry/lintel detail within this construction series; no exact final room is asserted. 159 paired sets of plumbing penetrations and niche preparation match153/154 stone slab, herringbone ceiling/floor and134 completed glass shower.85 shows same shower next to double vanity;109 is the same vanity/mirrors and round wall vent. 135 and136 are the same bathroom: identical tub/shower screen, white stone veining, rain head, gray vanity and toilet. Finish details and source-series continuity associate it with the modern house, but no wider fixed landmark independently links this secondary bathroom; flagged as moderate association below.
